latest.content:
24 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 0626W
Tungsten West PLC
24 September 2026
24 September 2026
Tungsten West Plc
("Tungsten West" or the "Company")
Exercise of Options & TVR
Tungsten West (AIM:TUN), the owner and operator of the Hemerdon tungsten and tin mine ("Hemerdon" or the "Project") in Devon, UK, announces that, further to the announcement dated 16 September 2026, it has received a notice of exercise in respect of founder options over 828,597 new ordinary shares of £0.01 each in the capital of the Company ("Ordinary Shares") (the "Founder Option Exercise"). The Founder Option Exercise will provide £8,285.97 of additional funding to the Company, which will be used for general working capital purposes.
The founder options were granted in October 2021 and are exercisable upon certain milestones being achieved. The Founder Option Exercise is pursuant to the Company having raised sufficient finance (whether in the form of debt or equity or otherwise) to recommence mining operations at the Hemerdon Mine for a mine restart.
The founder options are set out in full in the Company’s admission document dated 15 October 2021.
The 828,597 new Ordinary Shares to be issued to pursuant to the Founder Option Exercise will rank
pari passu
with the existing Ordinary Shares and application will be made for the new Ordinary Shares to be admitted to trading on AIM ("Admission"). It is expected that Admission will become effective and dealings in the new Ordinary Shares will commence at 8.00 a.m. on or around 29 September 2026.
Total Voting Rights
Upon Admission, the Company's issued ordinary share capital will consist of 1,352,644,508 Ordinary Shares and 257,075,833 B shares. Each Ordinary Share has one voting right each. The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in treasury, therefore the total number of Ordinary Shares and voting rights in the Company on Admission will be 1,352,644,508. With effect from Admission, this figure may be used by shareholders in the Company as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, the share capital of the Company under the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.

latest.title: Strategic Tungsten Supply and Offtake Agreement
latest.content:
23 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 8695V
Tungsten West PLC
23 September 2026
THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONTAINS INSIDE INFORMATION FOR THE PURPOSES OF ARTICLE 7 OF THE MARKET ABUSE REGULATION (EU) 596/2014 (WHICH FORMS PART OF DOMESTIC UK LAW PURSUANT TO THE EUROPEAN UNION (WITHDRAWAL) ACT 2018 ("UK MAR").
NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION IN OR INTO, OR TO ANY PERSON LOCATED OR RESIDENT IN, ANY JURISDICTION WHERE IT IS UNLAWFUL TO RELEASE, PUBLISH OR DISTRIBUTE THIS ANNOUNCEMENT.
NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION IN WHOLE OR IN PART IN OR INTO THE UNITED STATES, CANADA OR JAPAN.
23 September 2026
Tungsten West Plc
("Tungsten West", the "Company" or the "Group")
Strategic Tungsten Supply and Offtake Agreement with The Elmet Group
Eight-year agreement establishes major UK – US tungsten supply relationship
Tungsten West (AIM: TUN), the owner and operator of the Hemerdon tungsten and tin mine ("Hemerdon")
in Devon, UK, is pleased to announce that it has entered into a binding eight-year supply and offtake agreement (the "Agreement") with Elmet Technologies LLC ("Elmet"), a member of The Elmet Group, a US-based vertically integrated producer of tungsten products and advanced materials.
Highlights
Eight-year supply and offtake agreement with Elmet for 1,000 tonnes (100,000 metric tonne units “mtu”) per annum of contained WO₃ from Hemerdon.
Over £1.4 billion indicative nominal value at prevailing market commodity prices and foreign exchange rates.
At Tungsten West’s request, Elmet will use commercially reasonable endeavours to process an additional 500 tonnes per annum of contained WO₃ to support UK Government strategic requirements and UK industry.
Establishes a substantial long-term route for Hemerdon tungsten into US and UK tungsten processing and manufacturing supply chains.
Complements the UK Government's strategic interest in Hemerdon following the National Wealth Fund's investment of up to £71 million in Tungsten West and the associated exclusive negotiation period for the UK Government to procure up to 50% of Hemerdon's annual tungsten production.
Positions Hemerdon as an increasingly important source of secure, Western-produced tungsten for defence, aerospace, advanced manufacturing and other strategic industries.
Elmet is a global producer of tungsten and molybdenum materials and products, providing precision machining and engineering solutions for industrial markets. It is also a leading US owned producer of pure tungsten and molybdenum.
Blair McDougall, Minister for Reindustrialisation for the United Kingdom, said:
“This announcement builds on our partnership with the United States, working together in areas like mining and processing, helping crucial sectors like defence and clean energy in both countries get the
minerals
they need.
"This is our
Critical
Minerals
Strategy in action - forging ambitious international
partnerships that strengthen our economic security and help build more resilient, sustainable
critical
minerals
supply chains."
Jeffery Court, CEO of Tungsten West, commented:
"This is a landmark commercial agreement for Tungsten West and represents a major step in establishing Hemerdon as a strategically important source of tungsten for the Western world.
"The eight-year agreement outlines the supply of 1,000 tonnes of contained WO₃ annually and at current tungsten market prices, has an indicative nominal value of over £1.4 billion.
"More importantly, it establishes a long-term supply relationship between Hemerdon and one of America's leading vertically integrated tungsten businesses at a time when both the United States and United Kingdom are placing increasing strategic importance on securing resilient supplies of critical minerals.
"The structure of the Agreement also creates the opportunity to provide an additional 500 tonnes annually in support of UK Government strategic priorities and industrial demand.
"Hemerdon is uniquely positioned to provide substantial, long-term tungsten production from within the United Kingdom. With production now underway, the support of the UK Government through the National Wealth Fund and this long-term commercial agreement with Elmet, we are building a mine-to-market supply chain capable of supporting the critical mineral requirements of the UK, US and their allies."
Peter V. Anania, CEO and Chairman of The Elmet Group, commented:
“Our agreement with Tungsten West further builds upon the landmark investment we received from the Department of War and advances our strategy to build a resilient supply chain for the U.S. and allied nations.
“The Elmet Group and Tungsten West are firmly aligned in our commitment to securing domestic and allied production, supply, and consistency for customers across the full breadth of critical end markets.”
Further information
Under the Agreement, Tungsten West will supply Elmet with 1,000 tonnes per annum of contained WO₃ over the eight-year term of the Agreement.
Pricing is variable and referenced to European Ammonium Paratungstate (APT) pricing. Based on the prevailing reference price and the prevailing USD:GBP exchange rate, the Agreement represents an indicative nominal value of over £1.4 billion during its eight-year term. This figure is indicative and does not represent guaranteed revenue to Tungsten West. Actual revenue will depend upon, amongst other things, prevailing tungsten prices, foreign exchange rates, product specifications, quantities delivered and the pricing mechanism contained within the Agreement.
The Agreement also provides that, at Tungsten West’s request, Elmet will use commercially reasonable endeavours to process up to an additional 500 tonnes per annum of contained WO₃ for processing into down-stream tungsten products to support UK Government strategic requirements and UK industry, subject to the applicable commercial and delivery terms being agreed between the parties.
Strategic significance
The Agreement represents a significant commercial milestone for Tungsten West and establishes a long-term supply relationship between one of the world's largest tungsten deposits and one of the United States' leading vertically integrated tungsten businesses.
Elmet is building a vertically integrated US and allied tungsten supply chain, supported by a US$450 million committed investment from the US Department of War, and has separately secured an up to US$2 billion DLA contract to supply tungsten materials to the US National Defense Stockpile. Elmet has identified long-term mine offtakes as an integral part of securing the incremental tungsten feedstock required to support its expanded processing capacity and future stockpile deliveries. This Agreement is a key cornerstone of tungsten concentrate supply to enable this strategy.
UK strategic supply
The Agreement has been structured to preserve the ability for additional Hemerdon production to support UK strategic requirements.
In August 2026, the National Wealth Fund announced an investment of up to £71 million in Tungsten West. The investment also provides the UK Government with a negotiation period for the right to procure up to 50% of the mine's tungsten production as stated in the Company's 2025 Feasibility Study.
The additional 500 tonnes per annum WO₃ option under the Elmet Agreement provides further flexibility to support UK Government strategic tungsten requirements and UK industry while maintaining the Company's long-term commercial relationship with Elmet.
The combination of Hemerdon's scale, its location in the United Kingdom and the establishment of long-term commercial relationships with major Western tungsten processors positions the mine as an important component of UK and US critical-mineral supply-chain resilience.
ENDS
About The Elmet Group
The Elmet Group is a U.S.-based provider of precision-engineered components and advanced high-energy systems for the Aerospace, Defense and Government, Industrial, Medical, Semiconductor and Electronics, and Energy industries. The Elmet Group operates through three segments: Critical Materials Components (CMC), Engineered Microwave Products (EMP), and Elmet Refining & Trading (ERT), leveraging materials science and precision engineering expertise to deliver high-performance solutions. The Elmet Group is dedicated to strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities to support the U.S. and its allies’ needs in both critical materials and advanced high-power microwave systems.

latest.title: Processing operations commence during visit by NWF
latest.content:
15 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 7152U
Tungsten West PLC
15 September 2026
15 September 2026
Tungsten West Plc
("Tungsten West", the "Company" or the "Group")
Processing operations commence during visit by National Wealth Fund CEO
Tungsten West plc (AIM: TUN), the owner and operator of the Hemerdon tungsten and tin mine in Devon, UK, is pleased to announce that Hemerdon has entered production, with ore now being processed through the plant as the Company commences the next phase of its operational ramp-up.
The milestone was marked during a visit to Hemerdon by Oliver Holbourn, Chief Executive Officer of the National Wealth Fund, reflecting the strategic importance of Hemerdon to the development of secure UK and Western supply chains for critical minerals.
Hemerdon is one of the world's largest known tungsten deposits and represents a strategically important domestic source of tungsten, a critical mineral used extensively across a range of industries, including aerospace, clean energy, manufacturing of chips and semiconductors, automotive, defence and industrial applications.
Following the commencement of processing, the Company will progressively ramp up operations towards targeted steady-state production.
Jeffery Court, Chief Executive Officer of Tungsten West, commented:
"Hemerdon entering production is a landmark moment for Tungsten West and represents the culmination of an enormous effort by our team and partners to bring this strategically important mine back into operation.
"We were delighted to mark this milestone alongside Oliver Holbourn and the National Wealth Fund. At a time when governments and industry are increasingly focused on security of critical mineral supply, Hemerdon has the potential to become one of the Western world's most important sources of tungsten.
"Our focus now turns to safely ramping up operations and establishing Hemerdon as a reliable, long-term supplier of tungsten concentrate to the UK and its international partners."
Oliver Holbourn, Chief Executive Officer of the National Wealth Fund, said:
"Just a few weeks on from our investment, and we're already seeing the first tungsten ore being processed at site. Through our investment, we want to unlock this strategic asset for the UK, secure a domestic supply of tungsten for our industry and bring jobs and opportunity to local communities. With today's news, Tungsten West is delivering on the first step in that ambition."
Chief Secretary to the Treasury Emma Reynolds said:
"Tungsten West is a great success story for Devon and demonstrates our vision to drive growth in every postcode and the reindustrialisation we need for good jobs across the UK.
"Less than two weeks after announcing £71 million from the National Wealth Fund to restart operations, Hemerdon mine is already helping to create jobs, increase productivity and drive growth across the South West."
Jeff Court hosts a site visit with Oliver Holbourn, CEO of the National Wealth Fund, and Ingrid Edmund, Managing Director of the National Wealth Fund.
Oliver Holbourn, CEO of the National Wealth Fund, on a tour around the processing plant at Hemerdon.

company_30s.what_they_do: TUN.L is a mining and processing company that extracts tungsten ore and turns it into high‑purity tungsten products used in hard‑metal alloys, cutting tools, and high‑temperature components.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Tungsten is a critical metal for defence, aerospace, automotive, and electronics. Global demand is tightening as new high‑strength alloys and electric‑vehicle components need more tungsten, giving the company a clear market that is hard to substitute.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is in the ramp‑up phase: it has just commissioned a new processing plant, secured a large offtake agreement, and received a strategic investment from the UK government. Cash flow is improving as loan repayments are made and the plant starts operating.

rns_narrative: The company has just launched a new processing facility and is starting production, which should boost output by the end of the year.
It has signed a long‑term offtake deal that guarantees a steady customer base and has attracted a sizable government investment that will help cover initial costs.
Corporate governance moves – a joint broker appointment, major holding notification, and executive awards – signal that the board is aligning incentives and tightening oversight.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet but hopeful – people are listening for the first signs of production and a price lift.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Those who are optimistic point to the offtake agreement and government backing as evidence that the company is on track to turn around its deep crash.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Skeptics worry that demand could still be weak and that the new plant might face cost overruns or regulatory delays.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The mood has shifted from neutral chatter to a small but growing bullish thread, especially after the offtake announcement.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat – no recent spikes in public interest, which means a surprise catalyst could create a big swing.

near_term_catalysts: The first shipment from the new plant, expected in the next 60–90 days.
Official confirmation that the offtake agreement is active and that customers have placed orders.
A rise in tungsten spot prices that moves the company’s revenue outlook higher.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike that pushes the price above the recent support zone and a clear break of the 50‑day moving average. Any news that the plant is operating at full capacity will be a strong confirmation.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is still in the early recovery phase after a very deep crash. A tight compression in the price chart suggests that a breakout is likely if the supply‑demand imbalance turns in the company’s favour.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The deep crash has left the share price almost 90% below its peak, creating a huge upside if the price climbs back to 50% of that peak – that’s roughly three times the current price. The new plant and government‑backed offtake agreement give the company a realistic path to earnings growth, and the market has largely ignored these developments so far, leaving room for a surprise rally.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the plant runs into cost overruns or if tungsten demand stays weak, the price could stay near the current trough. A further decline to zero would wipe out the remaining equity, but that risk is limited by the already severe drawdown.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is about 3‑to‑1 compared to the remaining downside risk. A well‑timed entry could deliver a 200–300% return if the price reaches halfway to its all‑time high.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a clear break above the recent support level with a stop a few points below that support. Size the position so that a 20% drop would be the maximum loss on the trade.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for the first production run to hit the plant, confirmed by a volume spike and a price move above the 50‑day moving average. That will be the green light to enter.
playbook.if_passing: There are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy risks, so the setup remains attractive unless the company fails to start production or the offtake agreement falls through.

ai_insights.bottom_line: A deep crash has left TUN.L almost 90% off its peak, but a new plant and a government‑backed offtake deal give a clear path to a 3‑to‑1 upside if the price recovers to halfway to its all‑time high.
